{"id":"JMAP-ayoz.36","title":"MemoryBackend.objects_mut helper silently auto-registers accounts in known_accounts (workspace-wide cookie-cut)","description":"Discovered while fixing bd:JMAP-ayoz.2. The MemoryBackend helper

    fn objects_mut(&mut self, type_name, account_id) -> &mut HashMap<Id, Value> {
        self.known_accounts.insert(account_id.to_owned());
        self.objects.entry(...).or_default()
    }

silently extends `known_accounts` on every call. This is a workspace-wide
cookie-cut pattern present in the canonical jmap-mail-server (memory.rs line
148-ish) and propagated to chat-server, calendars-server, tasks-server,
contacts-server, sharing-server, and metadata-server (NOT filenode-server,
which uses a different shape).

Consequence: update_object and destroy_object against an unknown account_id
silently auto-register the account (then return NotFound for the missing
object). Even after the per-create fix from bd:JMAP-ayoz.2, the broader
'phantom account' surface remains via the helper.

Canonical-template propagation rule applies: fix jmap-mail-server first,
then propagate to all six siblings in the same pass.

Fix options:
1. Remove the silent insert from objects_mut; require callers to use
   register_account or new_with_accounts.
2. Rename objects_mut to objects_mut_or_register and add a sibling
   objects_mut_strict that returns None for unknown accounts; migrate
   callers to the strict variant.
3. Move the account_exists check up into the public API methods
   (create/update/destroy/get_state/etc.) and leave the helper alone
   but documented.

Recommendation: option 1 — remove the silent insert, fix any test that
relies on the side-effect (new_with_accounts already covers the common case).
The objects_mut helper should be a pure storage operation, not an
account-lifecycle one.","status":"deferred","priority":1,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-05-14T14:41:04Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-05-17T20:02:53Z","metadata":{},"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"","depends_on_id":"","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-05-14T07:41:03Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}
